subject: MATHEMATICS
applicability_conditions: learner must decide whether a foundational statement is a common notion or a geometric postulate
use when classification is driven by familiar wording rather than by what the statement asserts
anchor: A common notion asserts a general truth about magnitudes of any kind, while a postulate grants a specifically geometric construction or property.
ordinary_language_bridge: Ask 'is this about quantities in general, or about drawing and geometry in particular?' before naming the category.
reconstruction_route: paraphrase what the statement actually asserts
decide whether the assertion mentions a geometric object or construction
apply the common-notion criterion of general magnitude
apply the postulate criterion of granted geometric construction
name the category and state the deciding phrase

minimal_contrast.shared_structure: two statements of equal length in the same formal register
minimal_contrast.focal_distinction: a general statement about equal magnitudes versus a permission to draw a specific figure
minimal_contrast.prediction_prompt: Which statement would still make sense outside geometry?
minimal_contrast.decisive_feature: reference to a geometric construction is what makes a statement a postulate

misconception_discriminator.candidate_wrong_model: classification follows from how familiar or self-evident a statement sounds
misconception_discriminator.probe: offer an unfamiliar but general magnitude statement and a familiar construction statement
misconception_discriminator.decisive_response: learner classifies by assertion type and quotes the deciding phrase

repair_route: re-paraphrase each statement in plain terms
test each paraphrase against the general-magnitude criterion
test each paraphrase against the geometric-construction criterion
retry on a mixed set of statements
verification_method: restate the deciding phrase and confirm it matches the chosen criterion
check that no statement is classified on wording familiarity alone
known_limitations: does not settle historical variation between editions of the Elements
does not establish independence or consistency of the axiom set
